It is the combined cycle power block inside the site fence that the developer drew in its application to the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin. Where the site is: - The joint application for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity, filed November 6, 2026 in docket 5-CE-162, is at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=617707. On page 20 of the file, section 7.11.1, it says 'The Proposed Site is located in Section 04, Township 20 North, Range 20 East. The permanent footprint of the Proposed Site is approximately 85 acres.' - Section 7.11.2 on the same page says construction traffic will enter the site from County Road K. Where the plant sits inside the site: - Appendix L of the application is a zip file of mapping data, at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=617796. Its layer 'Proposed_Site_Footprint' is one shape of 84.8 acres. It runs from 44.22705 to 44.23355 north and from -88.12044 to -88.11390 east. Its layer 'Proposed_Site_Fence_Line' is the fenced area, from 44.22763 to 44.23347 north and from -88.11894 to -88.11426 east. - The site layout drawing in Appendix A, 'Proposed Site GA', is at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=617756. Page 2 of the file is drawing GA001, revision J, titled 'Forest Junction Energy Center Union Depot Energy Center General Arrangement'. It is drawn on an air photo. The five simple cycle turbines of Forest Junction fill the middle and south of the fence. The one combined cycle unit of Union Depot is at the north end, with its gas turbine, heat recovery steam generator, stack, steam turbine and air cooled condenser fans. - I laid the mapping layers over a satellite picture. The footprint matches the farm field north of County Road K, and the stormwater pond and the drainage swale line up with the drawing. Read against the pond and the fence, the center of the combined cycle block falls at about 44.23250, -88.11630. The imagery date is unknown, and the field is still bare farmland. - The point is shown on a map at https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=44.23250,-88.11630. Why the accuracy is exact: - The point rests on the site footprint coordinates filed with the application, and the plant's own block is placed from the developer's site drawing. That is the manual's route for coordinates in a permit application or a similar document. How far it moves: - The point moves about 6.6 km from GEM's point 44.19000, -88.05800, which is near Brillion. It is about 500 m from the middle of the wetland survey area that the first look used. The project is still pre-construction, with construction planned to start in Q4 2027 and finish in Q4 2031. The plan names a GE 7HA.03 turbine and 750 MW, matching GEM. No operator or combined heat and power statement was found in the plan. The move is over 2 km, but it rests on the applicant's own filed site footprint and site drawing, which both agree with the satellite picture, so no further check is needed.
